newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Jan-May insurance premiums up 11.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Jan-May insurance premiums up 11.7 pct.

text.p: Brazil's insurance premiums reached 7.2 billion reais in the January-May period, up 11.7 percent from 6.4 billion reais in the same period last year, the National Federation of Insurance Companies (FENASEG) said.
Fenaseg, whose figures are adjusted for IGP-M inflation, said in a statement that health insurance premiums rose the most, jumping 40.69 percent. It did not further explain the rise.
Automobile insurance premiums accounted for 31.5 percent of the Brazilian insurance market versus 21 percent for health and 18.4 percent for life insurance.
Claims totalled 66.6 percent of premiums in the five-month period compared with 60.8 percent in the same period last year.
The rise in claims was seen mostly in the automobile and health insurance sectors, which posted rates of 77.5 percent and 73.5 percent, respectively, it added.
Fenaseg technical director Maria Elena Bidino was quoted in the statement as saying the insurance sector is likely to post 20 percent growth this year compared with 1996.
"Based on the numbers we have today from the first five months, we could end the year with premiums revenue of 18 billion reais," she was quoted as saying.
